- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥ 0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.  
- When sentiment is consistently negative (≤ 0.33), model underestimates; increase forecast by 1–3% to align with mean reversion bias.  
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > true by >5%), model often overcorrects in next period; apply downward bias of 2–5% to prevent overshoot.  
- If true price deviates from 30-day moving average by >2%, model is likely lagging; adjust forecast to closer to recent 7–14 day average.  
- In cases where sentiment shifts from positive to negative (or vice versa) within 3–5 days, model fails to adjust quickly; apply a 1–3 day lag correction to forecast.  
- For 30-day horizon, model often underestimates downward trends; add 0.5–1.5% buffer to forecast if sentiment is neutral or mildly negative.
